requirement: A refusal reaches the person as a sentence with a next step: a page with a way back for a failed sign-in or an unavailable workspace, a named sentence for each seat, address, create and import refusal, and never a machine code

oracle.ref: PR #849 (fix); fix evidence: The same four files run against the base sources (811108bd2, extracted with git archive into a scratch copy): 400/460 fail, every failure an assertion on the reported behaviour (application/json or text/plain where a page is expected, the generic sentence where a named one is expected, a bare code on screen, a claim deleted on an outcome nobody confirmed) except three where a JSON null body makes the base wizard throw. The Add site file against the sources as they stood before the import-start outcome was made three-state: 177/213 fail, each of the 22 repaired behaviours by assertion. The Add site file against the sources as they stood before the site was looked at ahead of a start: 172/213 fail, each of the 13 repaired behaviours by assertion. The web file against this tree with only identity/route.js as it stood before `/verify` read the gate's `waitlist` status: 4/46 fail, exactly the 4 repaired behaviours, by assertion. All four files against this tree with the 19 sources of the sixth review round as they stood before it (a start under a claim that already stood, a DELETE after a status look, a retry link from a two-slash address, the 'invitation closed' title, a 5xx body read as a refusal): 77/460 fail, each of the 24 repaired behaviours by assertion. All four files against this tree with the Add site strings and its seven translations as they stood before the seventh review round (the claim-stands sentence named an earlier import and advised deleting the site): 8/460 fail, exactly the 8 new cases, by assertion. All four files against this tree with the My Sites row-errors.ts and strings.ts as they stood before an unnamed 4xx got its own sentence (it kept no 'nothing was changed'): 68/460 fail with today's tests, by assertion: the 5 cases of that repair, and cases of later rounds and of the merged target on the same two files. All four files against this tree with the seven refusal readers as they stood before each code was bound to the status its door sends it with (404 NOT_SIGNED_IN told as an ended session, 401 TAKEN as a taken address, a failed accept naming ALREADY_GRANTED as a quiet success): 115/460 fail with today's tests, by assertion: the 43 cases of that round, and cases of later rounds and of the merged target on the same files. All four files against this tree with the My Sites and Team refusal readers and the two string tables as they stood before the tenth review round (a 403 SEAT_NOT_AUTHORIZED on leave or delete told as a missing role, a 403 or 404 with no code of the door's guessed as one of its reasons, role sentences with no next step): 158/460 fail, by assertion: the 29 cases of that round, and cases of the merged target (its key names, its three removal kinds) on the same four files. All four files against this tree with the My Sites index.tsx as it stood before a dialog's answer was bound to the opening it was pressed in (one shared error for the list and all three dialogs; a late answer closed or wrote into whichever dialog was open): 10/460 fail, exactly the 10 late-answer cases, by assertion. All four files against this tree with TeamView.tsx as it stood before the seat-write reading was kept apart from Approve (Approve's refusals were read through the seat door's status and code table, unlike the target branch): 8/460 fail, exactly the 8 Approve-reading cases, by assertion. The counts above are of the last measurement, after `origin/develop` b21c158bc was merged and the Decline and late-answer cases were added; every case red on an older source is green on the fixed tree. On the fixed tree: 460/460 pass, 0 failed, 0 skipped. The cancelled sign-in and the card layout (#993), measured 07/10/2026 on `origin/develop` 28658227c before the fix: the real callback answered `error=access_denied` after a valid state with `signin.stateBody` for Google and for GitHub; in Chromium the text of all three pages began 1px from the card's edge (its border) in both themes at 1280px and 360px, and each page had two `<main>` elements. On the fixed tree the same measurement reads the cancelled sentence for both providers, 29px, and one `<main>`. The desktop app's question, its approved sentence and the denied page arrived with `origin/develop` 701919944 in the old markup: measured there the same way, their text began 1px from the card's edge and each had two `<main>` elements; merged into the fixed tree, 29px and one `<main>`. Local WordPress 403 installation-access replies: the mapping-and-React-render regression fails on the prior client with Joomla administrator guidance (12 pass, 1 fail, 0 skipped); the narrowed WordPress mapping passes all 13 import-problems tests, including Joomla and unknown-platform fallback checks.
oracle.invariant: Exit code 0, `# fail 0`, `# skipped 0`, for each of S1, S3 and S4. Every test named `F-S1-002:` about a cancelled sign-in passes: a callback from Google or GitHub with a valid state of its own browser, no code and exactly one `error=access_denied` is a 400 page whose sentence says the sign-in was cancelled at that provider and that nothing was changed, in each of the eight interface languages, with the link back to /login that keeps a safe `next`; it never shows the sentence about taking too long or another browser, nor anything else the provider sent (`error_description`, `error_uri`); it reaches no provider, writes no identity, sets no session and clears the state cookie; a fetch caller still gets 400 `{"code":"OAUTH_STATE_INVALID"}`; the state is consumed, so a replay, a later code for the same state and the loser of two racing returns get the state sentence; a missing code with no `error`, an empty, differently cased, padded, longer, repeated or bracketed `error`, any other provider error, or `access_denied` in another parameter keeps the state sentence; a callback that carries a code is exchanged as before whatever `error` says; `error=access_denied` with a missing, empty, mismatched, malformed, unknown, other provider's or expired state is refused as a state failure. S3: every test passes: `signInFailedPage` (each reason, with and without a provider), `deviceConfirmPage` (with and without a device), `deviceApprovedPage` (approved and refused, for a lane and for the desktop app), `desktopConfirmPage` (with and without a device) and `deviceDeniedPage`, in every interface language, have exactly one `<main>`, one `div.card` that is its child, only `.card-header` / `.card-content` / `.card-footer` as the card's children, and every heading, sentence, link, form and button inside one of those parts, which the shell pads; a reason or provider the page does not know is the state sentence and no name; a hostile `next` is never the way back; the approval form still posts the nonce to /signin/approve with no script; the desktop question posts the nonce to /signin/approve and to /signin/deny from two forms, shows the match code escaped and has no script; an approved desktop round reads the sentence that sends the person back to the app; addresses stay escaped and inside the email_off markers. S4: all 9 tests pass: in Chromium, with `prefers-color-scheme` light and dark, at 1280px and at 360px, each of the nine pages (the real callback's answer to a cancelled Google sign-in, the approval question with and without a device, approved, refused, the desktop app's question with and without a device, approved for the desktop app, denied) has one `<main>`, no sideways overflow, every heading, sentence, link and button at least 16px from the card's left and right edges, and a background and text colour that differ between the two themes. Every test named `F-S1-002:` passes: an OAuth callback refused for its state, its code or the provider's answer is an HTML page in the shared shell with a link back to /login for a navigation (400, or 502 when the provider cannot be reached), sets no session, shows nothing the provider said, and still answers `{code}` to a caller that did not ask for a page. Every test named `F-S1-003:` and `F-S1-004:` passes: a site's workspace that cannot be opened answers a navigation with the retryable page (503, the whole address kept) in the reader's language with no internal word, and a fetch with the same code as before; a form POST refused before it is passed on is told what it sent was not saved and is not offered a GET of it; an address that begins with two slashes is never handed back as a link or a redirect a browser reads as another host. Every test named `F-S1-012:` passes: a malformed /signin link, an unavailable provider, an unknown site and a refused hostname are translated pages with a link that leads to Tracy; a staff invitation not open for the signed-in address is a 410 page whose title claims only that no invitation is open for this address, that offers signing in with another address and returns to the same link, and one that cannot be checked (no database, or it does not answer) is a 503 page, never a closed invitation. Every test named `F-S1-013:` passes: with script on, INVALID_EMAIL shows the invalid-address sentence; a correct code for an address the beta gate itself (createBetaAccess over a stubbed membership service) answers `waitlist` for shows the not-admitted sentence and the configured whitelist link, on the form post and on the fetch; when the gate could not check (`unavailable`, `error`, or a status it does not define) the sentence says so and the whitelist link stays hidden; a member the gate admits signs in; a wrong, expired or exhausted code is told nothing about admission; the page's script reads a refusal only on the status the door sends it with (400, 401), never from a 5xx body. Every test named `F-S3-005:` and `F-S3-015:` passes: the invite wizard shows a different next step for NOT_SITE_OWNER, SEAT_NOT_AUTHORIZED and GRANT_UNKNOWN per site; a reply that does not account for exactly the addresses and sites sent, a refused site with no code or one the door does not write, an entry that does not say whether the email went, a lost answer or a 5xx (whatever code it names) is an unconfirmed outcome that re-reads the books, never the Sent step; Team, My Sites and the address form name an ended session, a lost seat, SITE_UNKNOWN, SITE_NOT_READY and NAME_NOT_RESERVED; a 200 with no verdict is not "taken"; no code and no internal word is shown; the address form reads the door's failures only on its 502, and the WordPress reason only beside ADDRESS_APPLY_FAILED there; a 4xx on a row action that no sentence names still says nothing was changed and to reload the page, while a 5xx or a lost answer claims no outcome. Every test named `S4-F002:` and `S4-F003:` passes: an ended session is its own refusal in the create and import wizards and comes with a sign-in link that opens a new tab; an unsupported choice and an idempotency conflict have their own sentences; the sentence for an unknown outcome never says nothing was created; HOST_UPDATING is the deploy's answer only on a 503; the other named import refusals have their own sentences; an import claim is a claim only on a 200/201 naming the site that was asked for, and a refusal only on a 4xx; after the claim and before any start the status door is asked by site key, and a read of that site and platform already going is followed instead of doubled; a start is sent only by the wizard whose own press made the claim (201) and only while every start it sent has a known end, so a claim that already stood (200) with no read to follow sends no start and shows the sentence that says why and what to do, and that sentence, in every interface language, names no earlier import and never tells the person to delete the site (the same 200 answers for a live site built on Tracy); no DELETE of a claim is ever sent, whatever the status door answered before; a start is refused only by the door's own 400 INVALID_REQUEST or 401 NOT_SIGNED_IN, after which the same wizard may start again; a start with no answer, any 5xx whatever code its body names, a 2xx without a run id or any other refusal is unconfirmed: no second start is sent, Start is not on screen, and the status door is asked by site key; only a run of that site and platform with every field its state needs, and that is not the run that stood before the start, is adopted (a running one is watched by its id, a finished one handed over exactly once); RUN_UNKNOWN, a failed run, another site or platform, or an unreadable status leaves a Check status action and never says nothing happened; a handover answered with a 5xx is not told as the refusal its body names; repeated presses send one request and an answer that arrives after the wizard closed does nothing; a malformed reply or a network failure is never a started build. In every refusal reader (invite, Team, address, My Sites rows and accept, create, import claim and handover) a code decides the sentence only on the status its door sends it with: a 404 naming NOT_SIGNED_IN offers no sign-in, a 401 naming TAKEN is the ended session, and a failed accept naming ALREADY_GRANTED is told as a failure. Decline has one exception, the pair its door sends: on `409 ALREADY_GRANTED` the dialog closes, the list is reread and the sentence above the list says the invitation was already accepted and that Leave site gives the seat up; the same code on 500, 502, 404 or 401 is told by its status in the dialog, which stays, and the list is not reread. Every test named `F-S3-015: a late Decline answer`, `F-S3-015: a late Leave answer` and the slow-reread case passes: an answer (or the reread after it) that arrives after its dialog was dismissed and another site's dialog opened neither closes that dialog nor writes into it; what it has to say is shown above the list, and nothing is sent for the other site. Every test named `F-S3-015:` about a 403 passes: on leave and delete `403 SEAT_NOT_AUTHORIZED` says the seat is gone (never a missing role), `403 NOT_SITE_OWNER` says the role does not allow it and whom to ask; a 403 or 404 without a code of the door's own is told with the neutral sentence that names a next step, in My Sites, on an accept and on a Team write; every role sentence (`error.notSiteOwner`, `settings.url.ownerOnly`, `backup.err.forbidden`, `backup.forbidden.content`) names a next step. Import problems use 12px regular status text and 14px icons. Blocking resolutions are open, warning resolutions fold unless an action is present. Failed copy progress stays visible, sign-in refusals stay by the account fields, manual-install links change the actual choice, and each customer-admin link retains its subfolder and secret query. Preflight stops at the first failed row; absent server evidence is never green. Resuming stores only siteKey, platform and runId. Restarting an unconfirmed import never sends a duplicate start or releases its claim. WordPress no_backend_access from the plugin-upload access probe renders the approved WordPress plugin-install guidance (Administrator role or installs disabled), with a WordPress Users link and no Joomla instructions. Joomla and unknown-platform no_backend_access retain their existing fallback. Import guidance headings: the lightbulb computed colour matches --warning and --dsw-alias-state-warn-primary; the shared title matches --foreground with weight 500 at the unchanged 12px size; body copy matches --muted-foreground. Every import resolution keeps My Sites in the app: its callback opens or focuses the existing dsh tab and never opens a browser page. Create and manual-install links retain their in-panel callbacks; all cases keep web destinations in new tabs. Site timeout uses three numbered steps and its Check again action stays in the footer next to disabled Continue. A running import shows one unnumbered safeguard without repeating the Follow it label; one-step guidance is a paragraph while singleton options retain bullets. INFO rows use the theme info colour. The committed client contains no local review switcher. Import error guidance uses in-panel manual installation, manifest version wins over stale run detail, manifest retry performs no import write, and admin links stay on their own CMS and installation path. The three named import-problems tests pass with no failures or skips: every guidance destination, link target and sign-in attribute matches English in all seven translated interface locales (vi, de, fr, it, nl, zh, es), including Joomla and WordPress admin-address variants. Semantic links resolve only known destinations and ignore translated href attributes; unknown destinations remain text. Join guidance links only to a safe local path and remains text when no join destination exists or the supplied path is unsafe. The import-wizard E2E suite exits 0 with no failures or skips, and the exact test `wizard renders an import handover and a failed build` passes. A single Continue click from the focused address input reaches the account fields on both the first import and the reset import; both imports hand over once, the reset clears credentials, and a failed build remains a failure.
